items.statement: After the switch, the proportion of patients arriving with a usable diary rises from about 67 to at least 85 percent, and fewer eligibility decisions are deferred.
items.rationale: The model's pick: completeness is the direct aim of the switch and was large in the crossover study (claim c5).
items.risks: Largely answered already by randomised evidence; does not address the manager's financial question.

items.statement: The switch costs the clinic more in nurse set-up time than it saves in appointment time and repeat appointments in the first six months, and it raises preventive drug spending by increasing the number of eligible patients.
items.rationale: Set-up time (claim c3) against shorter and fewer appointments (claims c1 and c2), with the drug budget as the largest consequence (claim c4).
items.risks: Six months may not reach steady state; drug effects lag.

items.statement: Patients aged 70 or over are less likely to have a usable diary after the switch unless paper remains available.

summary: Three hypotheses; the model selects h1.
